# Computer Project Management

Coursework for the *Computer Project Management* course at Wrocław University of Science and
Technology, 2026. **One fictional IT project — the Export/Import Management System — planned in
[[microsoft-project]] and matured across five lab stages**, plus a seminar deck on the non-technical
side of the discipline. 23 files: ~21 KB of prose and 588 KB of opaque binaries. No code, no build,
no manifest.

**Status: coursework, finished and frozen at last commit 2026-07-10.** "All finished and frozen"
(interview, 2026-07-28). Nothing here is maintained.

## The five stages

Each lab folder holds the same plan one technique later — [[numbered-stages-in-directory-names]]
applied to a document repo rather than a code one.

| Lab | Adds | Tasks | Duration | Finish |
|---|---|:--:|:--:|---|
| `lab1_WBS_Practice` | outline mechanics, FS links — a throwaway sandbox | 29 | 78 d | 15 Jul 2026 |
| `lab2_Task_Dependencies` | the real [[work-breakdown-structure]], FS/SS/FF, a 12-resource pool defined but unassigned | 38 | 110 d | 5 Aug 2026 |
| `lab3-4_Resource_Assignment` | the 9-person team assigned, over-allocation cleared by [[resource-leveling]] | 38 | 121 d | 20 Aug 2026 |
| `lab5-6_Baseline_and_Tracking` | a [[schedule-baseline-and-variance|baseline]], 7 control-point milestones, tracked actuals + `progress-report.pdf` | 45 | 134 d | 8 Sep 2026 |
| `lab7-8_Summary_Report` | the 8-page stakeholder report; **no new `.mpp`** | — | — | — |

The plan decomposes into 3 phases / 9 task groups / 26 working tasks / 7 zero-day milestones, runs
2 Mar → 8 Sep 2026, and ends at **190 960 zł, entirely labour** — nine hourly-rate work resources
against equipment, licence and material resources that carry no booked cost.

## The interesting part is the slip, not the plan

Between lab 2 and lab 5–6 the finish date moves out twice, for two different reasons, and both are
written down. Leveling costs 11 days; then tracking costs another 11.

> "The extra 11 days come from **resolving over-allocation**: once a resource can only do one"
> — Computer Project Management/lab3-4_Resource_Assignment/README.md, 2026-07-10

The second slip is a genuine planning decision with a rejected alternative:
[[sequence-integration-after-unit-testing]]. Its knock-on runs down the
[[critical-path-method|critical path]] into the finalization phase.

## The seminar is the other half

`seminar/it-pm-environments.pptx` (15 slides, Topic #12) covers what the labs cannot schedule —
PESTLE, EEFs vs OPAs, the socio-technical model, PMBOK vs PRINCE2, toxic team cultures, Brooks' Law,
the 4 Ps. Recorded as [[project-environment-factors]]. The repo itself states the split:

> "The labs are the **hard** side of project management — the WBS, the critical path, the
> budget. This seminar is the **soft** side"
> — Computer Project Management/seminar/README.md, 2026-07-10

Brooks' Law (slide 11) is the seminar arguing against exactly the recovery action the labs did not
take — adding a second Backend Developer to fix the over-allocation.

## Findings

- **11 commits in 48 minutes on 2026-07-10, zero fixes, zero merges.** A textbook
  [[import-finished-work-into-git]] dump; the last two (`e9eb6e2` MIT license, `4af85fb` license
  badges) land 43 minutes later and are pure [[presentation-polish-tail-commits]], byte-similar to
  the identical pair in [[physics-exam-prep]] (15:34:23) and [[privacy-policy-template]] (15:10:41).
  Per interview these dates are **consolidation, not release** — see [[import-finished-work-into-git]].
- **[[documentation-drift]], one instance.** `lab2_Task_Dependencies/README.md` says tasks are
  "linked with all four relationship types rather than a single chain" and then tabulates **three**
  — FS, SS, FF. Start-to-Finish appears nowhere in the repo. Whether SF was tried and removed or
  never applied is not recorded. `confidence: high` on the drift, `low` on the cause.
- **Binaries declared, but no Git LFS.** `.gitattributes` is four lines of binary markers:
  > "# Treat the binary coursework artifacts as binary — no line-ending"
  > — Computer Project Management/.gitattributes, 2026-07-10

  588 KB of `.mpp`/`.pptx`/`.pdf`/`.png` committed raw. Same posture as [[optimization-methods]],
  which commits an 11 MB PDF without LFS.
- **The READMEs are the deliverable.** Every lab folder is a reader-facing tour with tables,
  before/after comparisons and figures — [[readme-as-guided-tour]]. This is the only repo in the
  group where the README carries *more* substance than the artefact it describes, because the
  artefact is unreadable without Microsoft Project.
- **Variance is reported as raw deltas, not indices.** +11 d, +248 h, +14 880 zł. There is **no
  risk register, no PERT estimation and no earned-value CPI/SPI** anywhere in the readable files.
  See [[schedule-baseline-and-variance]].
